sections.overview: This small South American cichlid is known from the Amazon basin, especially the Tapajós drainage in Brazil.
sections.identification: Reported maximum lengths are 5.3 cm standard length for males or unsexed fish and 6.0 cm for females; the sources consulted provide little comparative field-identification detail.
sections.habitat: FishBase records it from freshwater rivers and describes it as benthopelagic; the available species account gives no finer microhabitat description.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet data were not provided by the principal account consulted, so a particular prey or feeding mode cannot be stated confidently here.
sections.behavior: The available species account gives no detailed behavioral observations, and aquarium occurrence is described as rare.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific spawning and breeding information was not available in the consulted profile.
sections.ecology: A 2005 phylogenetic analysis places Dicrossus and Crenicara together in a crenicarine clade; this links the present fish to the two Crenicara profiles in this bestiary, without implying that either is its direct sister species.
sections.conservation: FishBase displays a global IUCN category of Least Concern, assessed on 7 November 2018; that assessment should not be mistaken for a current population estimate.

sources.title: Morphology, molecules, and character congruence in the phylogeny of South American geophagine cichlids
